slides.say: For every three numbers x, y and z, diamond of x, y, z is equal to x to the power of y z, plus y to the power of x z, plus z to the power of x y. Diamond of one, one, and diamond of two, one, four, is equal to what?

A new operation of three numbers, but there are only numbers here, no unknowns. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, the standard way, and then with a shortcut that looks at the outer diamond first.

[short pause] There are two diamonds, so we work from the inside out, like with brackets. The inner one is diamond of two, one, four. So x is two, y is one, and z is four. Let's write the same template, with these numbers in their slots.

Each number goes to the power of the product of the other two. For the first part, the power is one times four, which is four. So two to the power of four, sixteen. For the second part, the power is two times four, which is eight, and one to any power is one. For the third part, the power is two times one, which is two. So four squared, sixteen. Sixteen plus one plus sixteen is thirty-three.

Careful, thirty-three is only the inner diamond, and it's waiting as choice number one. Now the outer diamond, diamond of one, one, thirty-three. One to any power is one, and that happens twice. And thirty-three goes to the power of one times one, which is one, so it stays thirty-three. One plus one plus thirty-three is thirty-five. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to look at the outer diamond before calculating anything. Its first two numbers are one and one. One to any power is one, so the first two parts are one and one, whatever the inner value is. And the last part is z to the power of one times one, which is just z. So the outer diamond is always two plus z.
So we only need the inner value, thirty-three, from the first method's calculation. Two plus thirty-three is thirty-five, choice number three.

Sometimes the outer slots make the inner value not matter at all. For example, diamond of z, zero, one, for a positive z. z to the power of zero is one, zero to a positive power is zero, and one to any power is one. That's two, whatever z is. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
